sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the great descent of the soul into this lowly world, which is ultimately for the purpose of an ascent to a level higher than before its descent, even to Atzmus.

translations.translation: And to understand this more particularly,
we must first preface the general matter of the descent of the soul below, which is a great descent from a high roof to a deep pit.
For the soul, before its descent below, is pure,
and there are several explanations of this,
One: that it refers to the World of Atzilus,
Two: the lower purity (Tahiru Tata’ah),
Three: the upper purity (Tahiru Ila’ah).
And its descent is to the very lowest,
not only to the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,
the worlds of separation in general,
but rather to this lowly world, below which there is no lower,
most of which is evil, with only a little good mixed within it,
to the extent that the deeds of this world are harsh, etc.
(as explained in Tanya
in the name of the Etz Chaim),
And furthermore,
the service in this world itself is in the very lowest place,
in the place of “for you descended to Egypt” and in the manner of “the evil inclination is among you,”
requiring one to wage war with the evil inclination, as “today it says to him ‘do this,’ and tomorrow ‘serve idols,’”
which is the opposite of “I am the L-rd your G-d” and “You shall have no other gods”
(the root of the 248 positive commandments and 365 negative commandments,
as explained in Tanya),
However, this descent is for the purpose of an ascent.
For even though the soul did not descend to rectify itself, etc., but rather to rectify its body, its animal soul, and its portion in the world
(as explained in Etz Chaim,
cited in Tanya),
nevertheless,
through the descent of the soul below, it is elevated to a level higher than it was before its descent,
above even the World of Emanation.
And even more,
to a level that has no comparison or connection to the matter of Hishtalshelus (order of descent), level, or rank,
to the extent that it is not even possible to say that it has a level relative to the order of Hishtalshelus,
but only in the known expression,
“to be absorbed in the body of the King,”
in His Essence and Being, blessed be He.
And in the language of the Zohar elsewhere,
in this level, “they are not found in the King except for Yisrael alone”
(which is above even Torah and Mitzvos).
And the ascent is through service in Torah and Mitzvos,
for “I was created only to serve my Master,”
and as it is written,
“And He placed him… to work it and to guard it,”
“to work it” refers to the 248 positive commandments, and “to guard it” refers to the 365 negative commandments
(for wherever it says “guard,” etc., it is only a negative commandment),
and this requires the preface of the Torah that “study is greater, for it brings to action.”
And also, conquering the evil inclination is through the Torah, as our sages said,
“I created the evil inclination, and I created the Torah as its spice,”
and “if this abomination meets you, drag it to the study hall,” etc.
And this is what is written,
“Turn from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it,”
which refers to positive commandments, negative commandments, and Torah,
as explained in Likkutei Torah on our portion
(Balak).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the soul’s ascent to a level incomparably higher than before is specifically through its work below, because it refines the lofty sparks from the World of Tohu that fell lower.

translations.translation: However, we need to understand the reason for the matter,
that specifically through the service of the soul below it is elevated to a level higher than it was before its descent,
even to an ascent that is incomparable to its previous level.
And the explanation is,
that the sparks within physical matters have their source in the World of Tohu, which is above the World of Tikkun.
And as it is written,
“For not by bread alone does man live, but by every utterance of the mouth of G-d does man live.”
And the Arizal explains,
that “the utterance of the mouth of G-d” in the bread is the G-dly spark within it.
And even though there is also within man an “utterance of the mouth of G-d” that gives him life,
nevertheless, he specifically needs the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” that is in the bread,
for whatever is higher falls lower.
And it is like the parable of a stone at the top of a wall,
when it falls down, it falls farther from the wall than a stone that falls from the middle of the wall, etc.
Therefore,
since the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” in the bread fell lower than the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” in man,
for bread is from the vegetative realm,
and especially at the time of eating it is no longer vegetative but rather inanimate
(and furthermore,
eating bread is with salt,
which is inanimate),
while man is a speaker,
this itself is proof that the source of the sparks found in the bread is higher than the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” in man,
even higher than the Supernal Man,
the level of Tikkun.
And therefore, specifically through them does man live,
the man below,
and
(through this)
the Supernal Man, as it were.
And to hint at another matter in this,
explained elsewhere
at length, the difference between the World of Tikkun and the World of Tohu,
that both were brought into being by the Supernal Will,
except that in the World of Tikkun it is in the manner of “this law pleased Me,”
and in the World of Tohu it is in the manner of “this law did not please Me.”
That is,
in the World of Tohu there is the Supernal Will,
but it is in concealment and hiding,
while what is revealed is the matter of the opposite of the Will, “this law did not please Me.”
And therefore, from this descends below,
that the matters that came into being from the World of Tohu,
although in revelation they are matters opposite to holiness, “this law did not please Me,”
nevertheless,
even within them there are sparks of holiness,
and on the contrary,
specifically within them there is the intensity
of the lights of Tohu.
And this is why through the descent of the soul below it is elevated to a level higher than it was before its descent,
for this is from the side of the refinements of the sparks of the World of Tohu,
through which one inherits the lights of Tohu,
which is the matter of “an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.”

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that negative commandments refine even higher sparks than positive commandments, because their fall is greater, and that repentance transforms sins into merits, drawing an incomparably higher light.

translations.translation: And so,
according to the above rule that whatever is higher falls lower, we must say,
that even within the sparks of Tohu themselves,
whatever fell lower has its source from a higher place.
From this it is understood that there is an advantage in the refinements achieved through negative commandments over the refinements of positive commandments,
for even though the sparks within physical things through which one fulfills a positive commandment also have their source in the World of Tohu,
nevertheless, the fall within them is not as great,
since they are permitted matters that are sustained by us.
However, with negative commandments,
which involve matters that are forbidden and bound in the hands of the external forces,
this itself is proof that the source of the sparks clothed within them is higher.
Therefore, through the service of negative commandments,
even at the beginning of service when one does not transform willful sins into merits but only pushes them away,
a more elevated light is drawn down than in the service of positive commandments.
And as explained in Likkutei Torah,
positive commandments correspond to Vav-Hei,
the level of “the revealed things,”
and negative commandments correspond to Yud-Hei,
the level of “the hidden things are for G-d”
(and also – Yud-Hei is a holy Name in itself),
and the difference between them is an incomparable difference.
And in general, it is the difference between internal light and encompassing light,
for positive commandments draw down internal light, which is light that is clothed in vessels,
while negative commandments draw down encompassing light, which the vessel cannot contain.
And this advantage of negative commandments over positive commandments exists even when the service in matters of negative commandments is only in the manner of pushing away.
And certainly when the service in them is in the manner of transforming willful sins into merits,
then one draws down a light that is incomparably higher even than the light drawn down through negative commandments in the manner of pushing away.
And it is understood from this that this matter of “willful sins become for him like merits” is only through the service of repentance,
for the regular service
(the continual offerings in their order)
in forbidden matters is only in the manner of pushing away.
And the difference between these two types of service is an incomparable difference,
as is understood from every place,
that the difference between them is like the value of the limited relative to the unlimited.
And as it is in the matter of time,
that the service of repentance is “in one hour and in one moment,”
above the measurement of time,
whereas regular service is measured in the continuum and expanse of time
(and consequently also in place).
